analysis:
This PR changes only provider launchd lifecycle plumbing. It does not change coordinator authorization, attestation, encryption or billing.

LaunchctlControl.swift (head lines 11-26, 54-56) adds two @TaskLocal test seams: runnerForTesting and homeDirectoryForTesting. They are internal, not public. Only @testable importers can bind them, and production never binds them. LaunchAgent plistPath()/logPath() now derive from LaunchctlControl.homeDirectory(), which defaults to the real home folder. WatchdogAgent and currentExecutablePath still use the real home folder.

LaunchAgent.restartAfterDrain now polls isLoaded() after bootout for up to releaseTimeout=60s before bootstrap. The poll is bounded, and on timeout loadService throws bootstrapFailed. This only improves availability (T-043/TB-003 lifecycle area) and does not widen trust.

ServiceDrain+Relaunch.swift adds relaunchDrainedProvider, which runs rearm() via defer. RestartCommand.swift and UpdateCommand.swift (head ~163-168) now re-arm the watchdog even when the relaunch throws. The watchdog's kickstartIfLoaded only acts on loaded jobs. It therefore should not resurrect a provider left unloaded by a failed bootstrap or stopped by the user.

One point I could not confirm because the source was not supplied: whether ServiceDrain.rearmWatchdog respects an intervening `darkbloom stop` or a cancelled update candidate. In the update failure path, rearm now runs before cancelPendingCandidateAttempt. If the job is still loaded with a candidate binary, the watchdog could relaunch it. This would follow the existing self-updater quarantine logic rather than any new trust path.

No serving authorization (TB-011) or attestation (TB-009) paths are touched. No security regression was identified.
